transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO, Hightower), Priya Singh (SRE), Jordan Park (Eng Manager)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/hightower-onramp (Redwood onramp deck), GDrive: https://drive.google.com/h/hightower-reqs (placeholder)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um we know you sent over the questionnaire, appreciate the detail. I'm Maya, I'm the account lead. With me is Liam, our SE who will walk through the more technical bits.
[00:10] Alex: Thanks Maya, yeah excited to sort through the options. We are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for two main products — the Insights chatbot (low-latency, lots of short queries) and the ReportGen pipeline (batch long-form generation + embeddings).
[00:22] Priya: Quick note - our compliance bar is high, we need audit logs, SSO (SAML 2.0), and option for KMS-backed encryption for private deployment.
[00:30] Liam: Absolutely, we generally see teams pick hosted for quick onboarding, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private when you need VPC/on-prem controls. We'll go through tradeoffs.
[01:05] Jordan: One immediate thing — we use LangChain in a few services, and LlamaIndex in another. We also have a proxy sidecar pattern today for token counting and rate limiting and we'd like Redwood to slot into that without too much refactor.
[01:20] Maya: Great, can you say a bit about how your proxy works today — is it an edge gateway, sidecar, or API gateway plugin?
[01:30] Priya: It's a sidecar that sits with our service, does token estimation, rate limiting, and calls out to HuggingFace-hosted models today. We want to centralize callouts so we can use Redwood behind a gateway to consolidate billing and observability.
[01:50] Liam: Ok so two integration patterns to consider: 1) keep sidecar and point it at Redwood's Hosted API, or 2) put Redwood behind your central gateway (we call gateway/proxy integration) and the sidecar just forwards. Both are supported. If you go Dedicated or Private we can support VPC peering or private link.
[02:30] Alex: For the Insights chatbot, latency is critical — p50 under 120ms ideally, p95 under 300ms. Can Redwood hit that with hosted?
[02:45] Liam: For small context sizes (~64 tokens) hosted can meet those numbers depending on model. But to be deterministic we'd likely recommend Dedicated pools sized for that throughput or private with local hardware. Hosted is subject to multi-tenant variance but we do performance profiles in the catalog.
[03:10] Jordan: How are tokens billed across our SDK calls? We wrap a lot of function-calling and streaming; does Redwood expose a token-metering hook to our gateway so we can account per-request?
[03:25] Maya: Yes we expose per-request token counts in usage logs and the console. For real-time enforcement you can query our usage API or use our token-meter webhooks. Also many customers instrument a lightweight call to the Redwood SDK to get the token delta before sending — avoids double counting.
[03:50] Priya: What about rate limits and quotas? We need burst capacity but strict monthly caps per team.
[03:58] Liam: We support per-key quotas, per-route quotas, and token-based quotas. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity and define burst pools that can be billed differently. There's also canary/fallback routing — if Dedicated pool full we can route to a cheaper model hosted fallback.
[04:25] Alex: Can you talk more about the routing fallback? If fallback hits, how's prompt fidelity impacted?
[04:33] Liam: Fallback routes to compatible model variants — for example, a quantized smaller model for cost-sensitive traffic. We expose metadata on the response so you can detect fallbacks and decide to re-try, degrade feature, or alert.
[04:55] Jordan: On the SDKs — we have services in Python and Node, and a couple in Go. Are your SDKs production ready for streaming and function calling patterns used by LangChain?
[05:05] Liam: Yes, our official SDKs support streaming, function calling, and structured output. LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations are used by customers; we have LangChain adapters, and a community LlamaIndex connector. Caveat — sometimes library API changes need small shim updates, but we version and publish examples.
[05:40] Alex: How about observability? We want tracing and metrics in our Prometheus/OpenTelemetry stack.
[05:48] Maya: We have OpenTelemetry headers in our SDK, exportable metrics to Prometheus exporters, and webhook hooks for events. Console shows per-route latency, token breakdown, and trace IDs that you can join with your traces.
[06:05] Priya: Any built-in probes for KV cache hits or batching efficiency? We'd like to know if automatic prefix caching is working.
[06:14] Liam: Yes we expose cache hit metrics, batching stats, and quantization profiles per model in the console. For Private/Dedicated there's deeper kernel-level telemetry we can enable for debugging.
[06:35] Alex: Could you run a micro-benchmark of our ReportGen workload? It's heavy embeddings (batch sizes ~128) and long generations (up to 4k tokens) — cost is a primary driver here.
[06:48] Liam: Sure — we'll need a sample payload and token distribution. If you can provide traces we can run using both Hosted (catalog model) and Dedicated (equivalent model) to show latency and cost deltas.
[07:08] Jordan: For embeddings we use LlamaIndex with a vectordb — we currently chunk documents to 512 tokens, batch 128. Any special best practices when moving to Redwood?
[07:18] Liam: We recommend locking model versions, using quantized variants for embeddings where quality allows, and enabling caching for repeated texts. Our Optimize tool can suggest batch sizes and quantization levels per workload. Also consider async embed pipelines to absorb burst.
[07:45] Priya: Security: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys for Private?
[07:52] Maya: Yes, for Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys. We also support VPC-only control plane options and air-gapped deployments in extreme cases.
[08:10] Alex: On the VPC side — we have strict egress rules and prefer private link. How does Redwood connect?
[08:18] Liam: For Dedicated we do VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. For Private we can deploy a control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package. We also support NAT-less egress for model weights when on-prem.
[08:38] Jordan: About the gateway pattern — we're concerned about header propagation for tracing and for function calls. Does Redwood preserve incoming trace IDs and return them in logs?
[08:47] Liam: We preserve incoming trace headers (W3C traceparent) and echo trace IDs in the console. SDKs auto-propagate, but if you use a plain HTTP proxy make sure to pass through the headers.
[09:10] Alex: A bit of an odd ask — our legal team asked whether Redwood supports per-customer data retention policies and can we disable model logging for certain routes?
[09:19] Maya: Yes, retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route. You can disable logging for specific routes or mask PII via our ingestion hooks. Private deployments give you full control locally.
[09:38] Jordan: For rate limiting enforcement, we want a token bucket at the gateway that counts tokens not requests. Can your webhooks supply a token estimate fast enough for enforcement?
[09:50] Liam: We have token-estimation endpoints that respond sub-10ms for short prompts — adequate for inline enforcement in most gateways. Some customers pre-compute token deltas in sidecars to minimize hop latency.
[10:12] Priya: Cost controls: we need team-level budget alerts and hard caps at month end — can that be enforced without downtime?
[10:20] Maya: We offer soft alerts, then hard caps that reject calls with a configurable error code. For mission-critical routes you can set fallback routing to a cheaper model rather than rejection.
[10:38] Alex: Any customers with similar scale to us? We peak at ~2k QPS for small queries during business hours, and background embed jobs spike at night.
[10:48] Liam: We have customers in the 1k-5k QPS range using Dedicated pools with autoscale. Autoscale config allows scheduled scaling for known windows plus rules for CPU/GPU utilization.
[11:10] Jordan: When you say autoscale for Dedicated, what's the lead time for bringing additional GPUs online? We can't tolerate long warmup for low-latency user traffic.
[11:20] Liam: Autoscale is fast for warm pools; we recommend a baseline reserved capacity for low-latency traffic and an autoscale buffer for background jobs. Burst capacity can be pre-warmed for predictable windows.
[11:40] Priya: Observability hooks again — can we stream logs and metrics to our Splunk/NewRelic?
[11:48] Maya: Yes, we support exporters (Prometheus), direct integrations with Datadog/NewRelic, and log forwarding via secure S3 buckets for Private.
[12:05] Alex: Implementation details — how invasive are SDK changes? Our LangChain code currently assumes OpenAI API shapes.
[12:14] Liam: We have compatibility layers and adapters that mimic OpenAI shapes for quick swaps, plus LangChain-specific modules. Rarely customers needed to change business logic. We can share migration examples.
[12:40] Jordan: About LlamaIndex connector — is it officially supported or community?
[12:45] Liam: Community maintained but Redwood has certified examples and we can support critical fixes during pilot. We also have a template repo to bootstrap connectors.
[12:58] Priya: Regarding function-calling and streaming, sometimes streaming chunk boundaries can break our parser — is there a way to standardize chunk sizes or newline markers?
[13:08] Liam: You can configure our streaming chunk sizes on the client SDK and we also support structured streaming with delimiting tokens to help parsers.
[13:30] Alex: Any limitations on model sizes for Private? We have a custom LLM (40B) and wonder if it can be hosted on a Private on-prem cluster with Redwood runtime.
[13:41] Liam: We support many sizes; for very large models we recommend specific hardware and we do a sizing exercise. Private lets you bring your model weights and we can assist with quantization and runtime tuning.
[13:58] Jordan: Security follow-up — can we require per-request mTLS from our gateway to Redwood?
[14:06] Maya: Yes, mTLS is supported for Dedicated and Private connections. Hosted API typically uses TLS + API keys, but we can discuss private link with stronger mutual auth.
[14:25] Priya: Who will own the pilot infra setup? We'll need an SE-led runbook.
[14:32] Liam: Redwood SE will own the pilot runbook and we can co-run the first deploy with your SREs. We'll create a checklist: credentials, VPC config, sample payloads, and success metrics.
[14:50] Alex: Success metrics — we'll define p50/p95 for latency, cost per 1k tokens for each route, and embed throughput.
[15:00] Maya: Perfect — we'll draft a pilot charter and share it.

[15:15] Recap and next steps:
- Redwood: SOC2 pack, architecture doc, pricing options, run micro-benchmarks (Liam).
- Hightower: provide request traces, token distribution, confirm stakeholders.
- Schedule pilot kickoff (2 hours) next week.

[15:45] Alex: One last quick Q — Do you have a recommended pattern for hybrid: use Hosted for non-sensitive traffic, Private for PII?
[15:56] Liam: Yes, smart routing rules are common: route sensitive routes to Private or Dedicated, public routes to Hosted with a cheaper model. The routing policy lives in the control plane and can be tag-based.

[16:10] Jordan: Cool. Thanks everyone — we'll review the materials and get back with the traces.
[16:18] Maya: Thanks all, I'll send the security docs and pilot charter after the call.

[16:30] (meeting wraps; end of recording)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional overlapping speech, some proper nouns mistranscribed (e.g., "Redwood Privatee"), speaker labels may shift in short segments.
